item.title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
item.dc:creator: Yifan Shen
Josey Hanish
Ishtiaque Ahmed Navid
Yuyang Pan
Zetian Mi
Theodore B. Norris
item.description:
Authors: Yifan Shen, Josey Hanish, Ishtiaque Ahmed Navid, Yuyang Pan, Zetian Mi, Theodore B. Norris
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. Here, we show that rapid lateral carrier separation in these nanostructures produces observable signatures in ultrafast spectroscopy. Using combined time-resolved photoluminescence and time-resolved differential reflectance spectroscopy, we observe photoluminescence exhibiting fast decay while differential reflection remains stable. This indicates rapid carrier separation. Studies of temperature and power-dependent photoluminescence confirm that carrier separation dominates over recombination-driven decay, and Mg doping studies reveal that stronger band bending enhances the carrier separation. The physical interpretation of the observations is supported by a numerical model including drift, diffusion, and thermal relaxation. The results provide critical insights into charge carrier dynamics in InGaN nanostructures, highlighting their potential for efficient photocatalysis.

item.title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Bischoff
Pavlin G. Poličar
Soham Mukherjee
Jakob H. Macke
Manfred Claassen
Cornelius Schröder
item.description:
Authors: Sebastian Bischoff, Pavlin G. Poličar, Soham Mukherjee, Jakob H. Macke, Manfred Claassen, Cornelius Schröder
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

item.title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
item.dc:creator: Stanley Fronik
Georg Wolff
Ronald W.A.L. Limpens
Anja W. M. de Jong
Shawn Zheng
David A. Agard
Abraham J. Koster
Eric J. Snijder
item.description:
Authors: Stanley Fronik, Georg Wolff, Ronald W.A.L. Limpens, Anja W. M. de Jong, Shawn Zheng, David A. Agard, Abraham J. Koster, Eric J. Snijder, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Upon infection, arteriviruses, coronaviruses, and other nidoviruses transform endoplasmic reticulum membranes into viral replication organelles. These include large numbers of double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) whose interior is considered the primary site of viral RNA synthesis. Early studies characterized nidovirus DMVs as sealed compartments, leaving it unclear how newly synthesized viral RNA could be exported to the cytosol. The discovery of DMV-spanning pore complexes in coronavirus-infected cells provided a plausible solution for this topological challenge. However, their structural organization, functional features, and evolutionary conservation across the nidovirus order, have remained unclear. Here, we investigate the macromolecular architecture of DMVs induced by two prototypic arteriviruses using cellular cryo-electron tomography. Despite the substantial evolutionary distance separating arteriviruses and coronaviruses, we observe DMV-spanning pore complexes with striking structural similarities to those previously described in coronaviruses. These pores may facilitate both export and encapsidation of viral RNA. In the absence of viral RNA synthesis, ectopic expression of the arterivirus transmembrane nonstructural proteins nsp2 and nsp3 suffices to induce the formation of pore-containing DMVs. Together, our findings reveal the conservation of key structural features of DMV pores across two distantly related nidovirus families and support a central role for these pores in nidovirus replication.

item.title: σ-complex stabilization shapes enzymatic C-glycosylation and restricts the scope of natural C-glycosides
item.dc:creator: Lluís Raich
David Teze
Gonzalo Bidart
Folmer Fredslund
Mandy Hobusch
Sonja Kunstmann
Natalia Putkaradze
Frank Noé
item.description:
Authors: Lluís Raich, David Teze, Gonzalo Bidart, Folmer Fredslund, Mandy Hobusch, Sonja Kunstmann, Natalia Putkaradze, Frank Noé, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11872
Abstract: Abstract C -glycosides are valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, yet their scarcity in nature and synthetic complexity limit their availability. Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C -glycosides, but few are known to display C -glycosylation activity and their mechanism remains unclear. Here, we study the intricacies of the maize C -glycosyltransferase Zm UGT708A6 using X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and atomistic simulations. Structural and dynamical analyses reveal two flexible gates that control substrate access and reactive conformations. Combined Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics simulations and mutational data support a stepwise S E Ar mechanism for C -glycosylation of neutral phloretin, mediated by the catalytic His-Asp dyad and involving a high-energy σ-complex that stabilizes through a water-mediated proton transfer. Complementary pH- and substrate-activity experiments, together with Quantum Mechanics calculations, indicate that substrate hydroxylation patterns, protonation states, and σ-complex energetics restrict the scope of C -glycosides. Our results provide a coherent mechanistic framework that reconciles experimental observations across diverse conditions and advances our understanding of enzymatic C -glycosylation.

item.title: Disaccharide production in marine cold seeps links dissolved organic carbon to anaerobic oxidation of methane
item.dc:creator: Lennart Stock
Gunter Wegener
John W. Pohlman
Laura L. Lapham
Karen G. Lloyd
Leketha Williams
Stian Torset
Ellen Lalk
item.description:
Authors: Lennart Stock, Gunter Wegener, John W. Pohlman, Laura L. Lapham, Karen G. Lloyd, Leketha Williams, Stian Torset, Ellen Lalk, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11875
Abstract: Abstract Anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) has been proposed as a source of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) at marine cold seeps, but the underlying molecular mechanism for its production remains unknown. Here we demonstrate a previously unrecognized link between AOM and porewater DOC by analyzing disaccharides in sediment and porewaters from a methane-charged cold seep in Astoria Canyon (Oregon, USA). In the AOM zone, sediments contain up to 17.7 mg L −1 trehalose with δ 13 C values as low as −78‰, and porewaters contain up to 1 mg L −1 sucrose with δ 13 C values as low as −66‰, representing 4.6% of DOC. Stable isotope probing experiments reveal AOM-dependent biosynthesis of trehalose and sucrose, and both disaccharides turn over faster than diagnostic lipids, suggesting that these compounds serve as biomarkers for active AOM. Accordingly, disaccharides mediate a relationship that may sustain microbial food webs and influence carbon cycling in methane-rich marine sediments.

item.title: Viscoelasticity of synthetic antigen presenting cells reprograms T cell metabolism for TCR-T cell manufacturing and therapy
item.dc:creator: Youcheng Yang
Yan-Ruide Li
Zeyang Liu
Hao Zhou

Xinyuan Shen

item.description:
Authors: Youcheng Yang, Yan-Ruide Li, Zeyang Liu, Hao Zhou, Yichen Zhu, Xinyuan Shen, Dexter Lai, Yihui Cen, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Adoptive T cell receptor (TCR)–based immunotherapy offers a powerful strategy to target solid tumors. However, how the physical properties of the antigen-presenting interface regulate T cell metabolic programming remains poorly defined. Here we develop synthetic viscoelastic activating cells (SynVAC), artificial antigen-presenting cells whose stress-relaxation kinetics are chemically tuned independently of stiffness and of peptide–MHC (pMHC) and co-stimulatory ligand density. SynVAC-pMHC provides a defined, scalable platform that outperforms monocyte-derived dendritic cells to enrich antigen-specific CD8 + T cells. Fast-relaxing SynVAC-pMHC amplifies TCR signaling and mTOR activity, drives metabolic changes, and programs antigen-specific T cells toward an energetically favorable state with improved memory-like features after expansion. TCR-T cells expanded using fast-relaxing SynVAC-pMHC exhibit superior persistence and durable antitumor activity in melanoma and ovarian cancer models. These results establish cell-mimetic viscoelasticity as a key biophysical cue governing T cell metabolism and differentiation and offer a fully synthetic strategy for manufacturing potent TCR-T cells.

item.title: Benefits and harms of antihypertensive treatment a modelling study in 5.5 million electronic health records
item.dc:creator: Ariel Wang
Constantinos Koshiaris
Niamh Gould
Lucinda Archer
Amitava Banerjee
Brandon K. Bellows
Christopher E. Clark
Andrew Clegg
item.description:
Authors: Ariel Wang, Constantinos Koshiaris, Niamh Gould, Lucinda Archer, Amitava Banerjee, Brandon K. Bellows, Christopher E. Clark, Andrew Clegg, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11496
Abstract: Abstract Antihypertensive prescription is guided by cardiovascular risk prediction models. However, existing models often exclude individuals with prior cardiovascular disease or those prescribed statin treatment. Consequently, there is limited evidence regarding how the benefits and harms of treatment vary according to an individual’s baseline risk. This cohort study includes 5,578,002 patients aged≥40years (mean age 59; 52% women) from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink between 1998–2018. A cardiovascular risk prediction model is developed using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink GOLD dataset and externally validated using the Aurum dataset. The model demonstrates excellent calibration and discrimination. Antihypertensive therapy is more likely to prevent serious major cardiovascular events (eight events prevented per 1,000 patients over 10 years, 95% confidence interval = 1 to 14), than to cause serious falls (two events per 1,000 patients, 95% confidence interval = −4 to 10). The risks of other adverse events indicate more nuanced or potentially harmful trade-offs. Here we show that a cardiovascular risk prediction model developed using routinely collected primary care data accurately predicts risk across a broad population of patients eligible for antihypertensive treatment. These findings will enable clinicians to better communicate individualised benefits and risks of antihypertensive therapy.

item.description:
Authors: Akisawa Satomi, Riho Saito, Kureha Satou, Yuan Ding, Nao Morimoto, Shuntaro Abe, Juri Yamada, Tadahaya Mizuno, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11328
Abstract: Abstract Symptom severity after viral infection varies among individuals, yet its mechanism remains poorly understood. We categorize mice into recovering and non-recovering groups based on body weight after infection with the same titer of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). We reveal that in the olfactory bulb (OB) where VSV initially expands, non-recovering mice exhibit an anti-inflammatory environment, suggesting its detrimental effect. Importantly, CXCR2 + cells resembling immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are more abundant in the OB of non-recovering mice than in that of recovering mice after VSV infection. Depleting CXCR2 + MDSC-like cells from the brain increases inflammatory responses and the animal’s survival after infection. Furthermore, site-specific labeling indicates that a significant fraction of these cells in the OB originate from the skull-bone marrow (skull-BM) as well as circulation. This study reveals the lethal effects of CXCR2 + MDSC-like cells on local immune responses to viral infection, highlighting their therapeutic potential for antiviral defense.

item.title: A framework-driven pathway to dehydration embrittlement in gypsum fault gouge
item.dc:creator: Nick Harpers
David Storz
Leander Fox
Arthur Ng
James Gilgannon

Roberto E. Rizzo
item.description:
Authors: Nick Harpers, David Storz, Leander Fox, Arthur Ng, James Gilgannon, Damien Freitas, Lisa Eberhard, Roberto E. Rizzo, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11873
Abstract: Abstract Mineral dehydration can alter the mechanics and hydraulics of fault zones and affects even plate boundaries, yet direct observations of how mineral replacement reorganises the architecture of a shearing fault gouge remain limited. Here, we combine a direct shear experiment with time-resolved synchrotron-based microtomography (4DSμCT) and digital volume correlation (DVC) to track shear deformation during the transformation of gypsum to its hemihydrate. The dehydration reaction progressively reorganises the load-bearing grain framework during shear, producing a transition from distributed granular deformation of gypsum gouge to localised brittle faulting of hemihydrate. By direct correlation between evolving microstructures and macroscopic mechanical and hydraulic behaviour, our results show that dehydration can induce a rheological transition, driving strengthening, embrittlement, and shear localisation even under drained conditions. Framework reorganisation therefore provides a direct pathway by which dehydration reactions may promote instability in fault gouges, complementing models that attribute dehydration embrittlement primarily to transient pore-pressure increases.

item.title: Hyperelastic microfibers as bioinspired proprioceptive artificial muscles
item.dc:creator: Joonhee Won
Jaehyun Jang
Hyunseo Kim
Inyoung Choi

item.description:
Authors: Joonhee Won, Jaehyun Jang, Hyunseo Kim, Inyoung Choi, Kyunghyun Jo, Yunheum Lee, Jiheong Kang, Steve Park, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Skeletal muscles combine forceful contraction with built-in sensing of their own length and movement, known as proprioception. Reproducing this combination in soft artificial muscles remains difficult, because added sensors often reduce actuation performance, complicate fabrication or limit miniaturization. In natural muscle, specialized sensory fibers are embedded alongside, and mechanically coupled to, the force-generating fibers. Inspired by this arrangement, we pair a hyperelastic, highly stretchable fluid channel with a stiffer, off-center optical core inside a single thin fiber. When liquid is pumped in, the channel wall undergoes a shape bifurcation: a localized bulge forms and propagates along the fiber. Because the core resists stretching, the bulge bends the fiber into a contracting coil, while the core also reports the fiber’s shape through the light it transmits. Here we show that such fibers, produced continuously by a scalable drawing process, act as artificial muscles that sense their own contraction and stretching, supporting self-monitoring movement in soft robots.

item.description:
Authors: Xing Wang, Huiyuan Xie, Yiyan Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Huimin Chen, Holli Sargeant, Felix Steffek, Jie Shao, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11605
Abstract: Abstract Large language models may facilitate unlawful activities, yet this risk remains underexplored in studies assessing illicit-content recognition or narrow categories of illicit scenarios. We define complicit facilitation as model guidance that assists users with illicit instructions. To assess it, we develop a legally-informed, automated pipeline grounded in real-world cases and legal frameworks, and introduce EVIL, a benchmark covering 269 illicit scenarios and 50 illicit intents across Chinese and United States legal contexts. Evaluations indicate that complicit facilitation is widespread across models, with legal warnings and lawful alternatives often omitted. Risks vary across socio-legal contexts and are elevated for crimes against societal interests, non-violent offenses, and intents involving subjective motives or deceptive justifications. Models provide more complicit assistance when instructions describe users as older adults, racial minorities, non-religious individuals, or workers in lower-prestige occupations. Existing open-source safety benchmarks and alignment datasets offer limited coverage and mitigation of these risks.

item.description:
Authors: Linmei Zhao, Mengling He, Wankai Ma, Zequan Xiang, Huaming Tao, Lijuan Song, Shaoyu Mai
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH 2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF 1 antagonist, CP-376395.

item.title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
item.dc:creator: Anna Barwinska-Sendra
Paula S. Salgado
Kacper M. Sendra
item.description:
Authors: Anna Barwinska-Sendra, Paula S. Salgado, Kacper M. Sendra
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11797
Abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm ( Bacillaceae , Peptostreptococcaceae ) and diderm ( Caulobacteraceae , Deinococcaceae ) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales , including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

item.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
item.dc:creator: Samuel E. Barnett
Ashley Shade
item.description:
Authors: Samuel E. Barnett, Ashley Shade
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

Abstract: Abstract Phenylethanoid glycosides are structurally diverse natural products widely found in traditional medicinal plants and display a broad range of biological activities. However, systematic studies of their functions and structure–activity relationships have been limited by inefficient access to diverse analogs in useful quantities. Two glycosylations and two additional transformations can be performed sequentially in one pot, substantially streamlining assembly. Biological evaluation in a TGF-β-induced fibroblast model reveals structure–activity relationships, provides insight into signaling pathways associated with antifibrotic activity, and identifies several compounds as promising leads for further antifibrotic studies.

Abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

item.description:
Authors: Amy Heshmati, Sol P. Juárez
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11639
Abstract: Abstract Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

Abstract: Abstract Chiral molecules interact with light so weakly that discriminating enantiomers or driving enantioselective chemistry by using optical approaches requires intense circularly polarised lasers or complex resonant structures. The resulting substrate generates superchiral fields that neither individual component produces. Raman asymmetries approach the theoretical maximum ( ≈ 2), while enantiomeric excesses exceed 25%. Finally, a six-order-of-magnitude enhancement over conventional Raman optical activity was calculated.

Abstract: Abstract A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BO x inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal Co F/H-1.0 @BO x catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BO x -Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11836
Abstract: Abstract Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale deuterium ( 2 H) NMR spectroscopy using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, yielding characteristic quadrupolar powder line shapes that are present in conventional bulk NMR spectra. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Powder-like NV-detected 2 H NMR establishes a powerful tool for probing molecular dynamics on the nanoscale - capabilities beyond those of most existing spectroscopic techniques.

Abstract: Abstract Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete oxidation and limited energy utilization. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al– x Ce powders develop an interconnected Al 11 Ce 3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al 11 Ce 3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO 2- x /CeO 2 -containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al– x Ce alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics.

Abstract: Abstract Toroidal vortices in fluid and gas dynamics underpin a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, from elementary particle physics to condensed matter systems, and have recently garnered significant attention in optics because of their inherent topological stability. Here we report the experimental observation of toroidal vortices in stochastic optical wavefields with partial coherence, termed coherence toroidal vortices, which eliminates deterministic topological signatures in conventional optical degrees of freedom while unveiling statistically hidden correlation topologies. These underlying topologies—including both fundamental and higher-order hopfionic textures—emerge in second-order field correlations and are accessible only through statistical measurements. We further examine the impact of chaotic channels on the stability of these statistically veiled correlation topologies, demonstrating that their topological invariants remain robust under realistic environmental perturbations. These findings are experimentally validated and offer novel insights into the potential of toroidal light vortices serving as controllable channels for directional energy and information transfer within complex media.

Abstract: Abstract Global climate forcing drives major changes in the North African summer monsoon (NASM), yet how high-latitude cryospheric changes influence tropical hydroclimate through atmospheric dynamics remains unclear. Integrating paleoclimate proxy evidence with coupled climate-model simulations, sensitivity experiments, and idealized atmospheric modeling, we show that Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) retreat acts as a dynamically important amplifier of NASM rainfall. Using the mid-Pliocene as a natural experiment for sustained global warming, we find that NASM rainfall was markedly stronger than that simulated under transient future warming for comparable global-mean temperature increases. GrIS retreat enhances Arctic warming, thereby perturbing the upper-tropospheric westerly jet and triggering a stationary Rossby wave train linking Greenland to North Africa. This polar–tropical atmospheric teleconnection strengthens monsoon circulation and moisture convergence, producing wetter conditions across the Sahara–Sahel. These results reveal a high-latitude pathway through which slow cryospheric changes modulate low-latitude monsoon variability under sustained warming.

Abstract: Abstract Maintenance of plant CG DNA methylation requires VARIANT IN METHYLATION (VIM) proteins, a family of E3 ligases that couple hemimethylated CG (hemiCG) with histone ubiquitylation to regulate MET1-mediated DNA methylation. How the hemiCG readout guides VIM proteins for histone ubiquitylation remains unclear. Here we report structure-function characterization of VIM1-mediated histone ubiquitylation, revealing the N-terminal tails of H3 and H4 as the VIM1 substrates. The structures of VIM1 complexed with hemiCG-containing nucleosome and/or E2 UBC11 reveal that VIM1 is positioned over the nucleosome disk surface, with the RING2 and SRA domains anchored to the H2A-H2B acidic patch and linker hemiCG site, respectively, and the RING1 domain mediating UBC11 loading. The RING2-mediated anchoring helps position RING1 near the H3/H4 tails for substrate access, while the SRA-mediated anchoring antagonizes an autoinhibitory state. Together, such dual nucleosome anchoring by RING2-SRA mechanistically links the position-varying hemiCG mark to persistent, yet context-dependent H3/H4 ubiquitylation.

Abstract: Abstract Nature-inspired designs for surface micro- and nanostructures have long attracted attention for their potential multifunctionality. This study introduces a mushroom-shaped silicone re-entrant structure achieved through a one-step, in-situ dynamic Droplet-Assisted Growth and Shaping strategy. The unique shape and multicomponent hybrid properties of the inert rod base and chemically modifiable spherical head of these silicone micro-mushrooms (SMMs) provide exceptional surface wetting and adhesion characteristics. The wetting states of these surfaces can be easily altered through O 2 -plasma treatment with the reconstruction of secondary and tertiary hierarchical nanostructures. item.description:
Authors: Saloni Sharma, Margaret S. Livingstone
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Experience-dependent plasticity in early sensory cortex is restricted to critical periods early in development. Whether plasticity in higher-order cortex is similarly restricted remains unclear. In the primate ventral visual stream, face-selective cortex emerges with experience during development, providing a powerful system to test how the timing of experience shapes higher-order representations. Using three male rhesus macaques selectively deprived of early face experience followed by prolonged normal face exposure, we found that face-experience-deprived monkeys acquire face-directed viewing behavior and neural face selectivity. However, they showed atypical within-face viewing patterns, while their neural representations retained lasting signatures of early deprivation, including selectivity for both faces and hands and reduced discrimination for face identity, expression, and viewpoint. Thus, higher-order visual cortex remains plastic beyond early development, yet the timing of experience fundamentally constrains the refinement of later-acquired neural representations.

item.title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
item.dc:creator: Wei Zhang
Tao Wang
Guilin Liu
Zhongfa Zhou
Duck Young Kim
Yu He
item.description:
Authors: Wei Zhang, Tao Wang, Guilin Liu, Zhongfa Zhou, Duck Young Kim, Yu He
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Core-mantle interactions are essential for understanding Earth’s interior dynamics and evolution. Experimental studies reveal that core-mantle reactions produce iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O (periclase‑wüstite solid solution). Here we show that Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O exhibits pronounced superionic-onset and grain-boundary premelting behavior above ~0.9 T m ( T m : melting temperature). These effects are significant in (Fe x Mg 1-x )O (x > 0.8) under core-mantle boundary (CMB) conditions, causing elastic softening, enhanced elemental transport, and ultra-low viscosity. Enhanced diffusion may facilitate core-mantle reactions and the accumulation of Fe-rich material near the CMB, potentially contributing to a dense basal assemblage. Under mantle flow and/or thermal buoyancy, the low viscosity of connected Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O could favor deformation and redistribution toward shallower depths. This process may contribute to the formation and evolution of some ultra-low velocity zones (ULVZs). The proposed scenario is consistent with the layered structures and inferred low viscosity of some ULVZs and suggests a potential role for Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O in core-mantle material exchange and heat transfer.

item.description:
Authors: Dandan Zheng, Changxu Liu, Qiang Yang, Yongqi Zhao, Shuangchun Wen, Hailu Luo, Shizhen Chen
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional materials exhibit pronounced layer-dependent properties, making accurate determination of atomic-layer thickness essential. Existing characterization techniques typically rely on spectroscopic signatures or scanning probes, which require complex instrumentation and often lack direct real-space interpretability. Here we introduce a spin-dependent optical differentiation approach that encodes thickness into directly observable edge features. By engineering the optical transfer function at planar interfaces, we access anisotropic and isotropic differentiation regimes governed by the spin Hall effect of light. In the anisotropic regime, the layer number is continuously encoded in the orientation of edge features. In the isotropic regime, a morphology-based transition, from disk to ring, provides a discrete and robust signature for layer identification. We experimentally demonstrate layer-resolved imaging in graphene, MoS 2 , and WSe 2 . Our results establish spin-dependent optical differentiation as a simple and versatile platform for translating atomic-scale variations into directly accessible optical features, enabling rapid and in situ characterization of two-dimensional materials.

item.description:
Authors: Tiansheng Bai, Yiming Hu, Wei Zhai, Xiongwei Zhong, Jinru Huang, Jiaxian Wang, Wei Song, Teng Rao, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11801
Abstract: Abstract The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium–oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Here, we report an artificial intelligence-integrated framework leveraging interpretable machine learning and density functional theory to navigate a vast chemical space of thousands of active sites. This approach identifies Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts as a better configuration among the selected elements for orchestrating multi-electron transfer. Theoretical analysis reveals that synergistic electronic coupling between the dual-sites fundamentally reconfigures the d -band center, thereby lowering the thermodynamic barriers for oxygen redox. Moreover, the catalysts enable precise regulation of the reaction pathway, inducing a controllable transition from the conventional two-electron pathway to a four-electron pathway. This shift yields a discharge capacity of ~60,000 mAh g −1 . Beyond its role as a positive electrode catalyst, this architecture functions as a multifunctional interfacial protective layer that stabilizes the lithium metal negative electrode by suppressing dendrite growth. Consequently, the lithium–oxygen system achieves stable lifespan of 2075 cycles under the four-electron pathway with reduced voltage decay. This work establishes a data-guided strategy for the rational design of atomic-scale architecture via artificial intelligence, unlocking the potential of multi-electron oxygen chemistry for lithium–oxygen batteries.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are generally committed to the hematopoietic lineage, but how that commitment is maintained is not well understood. Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While conceptually, higher-dimensional approaches such as 4D and 5D correlation spectra are capable of exceeding the established molecular-weight limitations by ameliorating signal overlap, their intrinsic implications for sensitivity and measurement times required have severely limited these important prospects in practice. Here we show that in high-dimensional experiments, the extensive use of dedicated transverse-mixing optimal control pulses (TROPs) can reduce the necessary measurement time by almost an order of magnitude. TROP’ed non-uniformly sampled experiments not only benefit from a multiplicative sensitivity enhancement in each complex time point due to concomitant transfer of both components of complex signals along multi-step magnetization transfer pathways, but additionally from facilitation of reconstruction with better raw data. Aided by the processing framework provided to future users here, the combination of an extensive use of TROPs with increased dimensionality hence presents itself as highly promising to ameliorate the conventional limitations of solid-state NMR.

Authors: Hwiho Kim, Sebastian Kunze, Kyungho Yoon, Sooseong Hwang, Yujeong Hwang, Jiseok Kim, Dongil Kang, Ikcheon Na, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Anodeless all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers offer high energy density and long cycle life, yet their operation in cold environments remains limited by poorly understood failure mechanisms. We demonstrate that a brief initial charge at 45 °C permanently activates the interlayer via Li-Ag alloy formation, enabling efficient Li transport even at 5 °C. Full pouch cells following this activation protocol retain 87% of their initial capacity after 250 completed cycles following one formation cycle at 5 °C. After 250 cycles at 5 °C, AAP-treated cells delivered approximately three times the discharge capacity of cells cycled with the fixed-temperature protocol. Such in situ electrochemical alloy activation offers a practical and scalable approach to extend anodeless all-solid-state battery performance to sub-ambient temperatures without material redesign.

Abstract: Abstract Polymer–solvent–nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid–liquid phase separation. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

Abstract: Abstract Beige and white adipocytes reside within the same fat depots but differ in their responses to β-adrenergic stimulation. Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11800
Abstract: Abstract Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.
